title: Gamaliel's advice (Acts 5:34–39)
hook: if it's of men it will fail, if of God you can't stop it

segments.voice: Yesterday, ekklēsia, the assembly shaken by a hard story Luke kept. Your line was the bible keeps the hard stories.

Voices are rising in a meeting. Someone is ready to fire someone. Then an older colleague raises a hand: wait. Let's not decide this today. Give it six months and see. The apostles have been arrested again, and again they've kept preaching. Back before the council, Peter says, we ought to obey God, rather than men. The council is furious; Luke says some of them want to kill the apostles. Then a man stands up and asks for the room.
screen: `THE ONE WHO SAYS, WAIT.` → `ARRESTED AGAIN.` → `A MAN ASKS FOR THE ROOM.`

segments.voice: Luke introduces him with respect: a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, honored by all the people. Later in Acts, Paul says he was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel. And the Mishnah, the great early collection of Jewish teaching, says that when Rabban Gamaliel the Elder died, the glory of the Torah ceased. He has the apostles taken outside and speaks to his colleagues. He reminds them of a Theudas who gathered about four hundred followers, and a Judas of Galilee who stirred people up in the days of the census. Both were killed; their movements scattered and came to nothing. Then, in the Douay-Rheims: "for if this council or this work be of men, it will come to nought; But if it be of God, you cannot overthrow it, lest perhaps you be found even to fight against God." The council listens. Instead of a death sentence, the apostles are beaten, ordered again not to speak in Jesus's name, and released. And Luke says they leave rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for the name. Gamaliel isn't a follower of Jesus here. He's a careful, devout teacher of his own tradition giving honest advice: don't force it; let God and time show what this is. Christians have often reached for his test when something new appears in the Church: a movement, an order, an idea. Some religious communities that began under suspicion, or were even disbanded for a time, were later recognized because they lasted and bore fruit.
screen: `A PHARISEE, HONORED BY ALL.` · `THEUDAS AND JUDAS: CAME TO NOTHING.` · `IF IT BE OF GOD.` · `LET TIME SHOW WHAT IT IS.` · then, large: `GAMALIEL'S ADVICE.`

segments.voice: Think of something you're in a hurry to judge: a new person at work, a change at church or in your family, a plan someone else is excited about. Notice the urge to settle it now, then picture setting it on a shelf with a date on it, three months away. If you pray, hold Gamaliel's words, if it be of God, and leave the outcome there; if you don't, just let it wait.
Gamaliel's advice. A respected Pharisee tells the council to leave the apostles alone: if this is of God, you can't stop it. Today's word.
Your line: if it be of god. Time has a way of showing what lasts. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Church often waits years before approving a new religious community or a claimed private revelation, testing it over time by its fruits and its fidelity.

fork.setup: you're on the council. the apostles keep preaching after you've forbidden it, and some want them dead. what does Gamaliel advise?
options: leave them alone; if it's of God you can't stop it.
fork.reveal: if it be of men, it will come to nought; but if it be of God, you cannot overthrow it, lest you be found to fight against God.

original.note: Greek: fighters against God (Acts 5:39), the danger Gamaliel warns of.

trapdoor: what you thought: an enemy of the Church who happened to help.
what it means: a devout and respected teacher of the law giving honest advice: let God and time show what this is.
what a scholar hears: the Mishnah (Sotah 9:15) honors Rabban Gamaliel the Elder; Josephus dates a Theudas later than this speech, a long-discussed puzzle.

chat.says: Who was Gamaliel, and what did he tell the council to do with the apostles?
options: A respected Pharisee who said: if this is of God, you can't overthrow it, so let them go.
A Roman governor who warned the council that only Rome could sentence anyone.
A Pharisee who urged the council to put the apostles to death before it spread.
chat.meaning: Gamaliel, a Pharisee honored by all, warned: if this work is of men, it will fail; if it is of God, you cannot overthrow it.

Gamaliel.meaning: a Pharisee and teacher of the law, honored by all

Mishnah.meaning: the great early collection of Jewish teaching

Torah.meaning: the Law, the heart of Jewish teaching

Theudas.meaning: a man whose four hundred followers scattered

notes: 'We ought to obey God, rather than men' (5:29) given without quotation marks; close to Douay wording.
Mishnah Sotah 9:15 on Rabban Gamaliel the Elder: paraphrased. Confirm.
Theudas chronology (Josephus, Antiquities 20.97–98, c. 44–46 AD) placed in the trapdoor only. Confirm phrasing.
Gamaliel framed positively and in his own tradition; Christian legends of his later conversion are deliberately omitted. Keeper may decide whether to mention them.
General claim about religious communities suppressed and later approved (e.g. the Jesuits, 1773–1814) left unnamed. Confirm.
